title: Latency-informed GeoRouter with Network Degradation Signals
creator: Sana Patel
description:
Problem:
We need a single-region selection service (GeoRouter) that combines short- and long-tail latency signals (p50/p95) with network-quality telemetry (packet loss, TCP RTO spikes, and hop changes) to produce a composite availability weight per POP/region. Current region arbitration uses either latency or coarse health indicators, which results in noisy route flapping during transient network degradations and suboptimal fallbacks to lower-tier model variants that increase cost and/or degrade quality.

Goals:
- Produce a stable, interpretable composite score that balances median and tail latency with network health.
- Avoid unnecessary failovers for short-lived spikes (hysteresis + decay).
- Route requests by policy: prefer region with lowest composite weight within the customer's allowed tiers, with graceful fallback to variant models when region capacity/health drops.
- Provide observability (per-region score and decision trace) and a safe rollout plan.

Design proposal (summary):
1) Signals ingested: p50 and p95 request latency windows (30s rolling), EWMA packet loss (1m), TCP RTO spike rate (1m), and inter-POP route changes (5m).
2) Normalization: convert each signal to a 0..1 normalized penalty using historical baselines and percentile clipping. Baselines are computed per-region and per-customer tier (to account for POP-specific latency distributions).
3) Composite weight = alpha * normalized_p50 + beta * normalized_p95 + gamma * normalized_net_health, where normalized_net_health = max(packet_loss_penalty, rto_spike_penalty, route_change_penalty).
   - Initial coefficients: alpha=0.25, beta=0.50, gamma=0.25. (Rationale: we bias slightly toward tail latency while letting network instability dominate when severe.)
4) Hysteresis & decay: when a region's composite weight crosses the failover threshold, mark as "degrading" and start a 30s confirmation window. On confirmation, route real traffic with a gradual split (80/20) into fallback variants for 120s before full cutover. After the event, use a 2-min decay window to prevent oscillation.
5) Tier-aware selection: routing policy evaluates regions in order of composite weight but restricts to same customer tier first (e.g., dedicated pools). If no region in the tier passes pass/fail thresholds, allow cross-tier fallback with explicit cost-metering and notify Console.
6) Variant fallback: when routing decides to fallback to a variant model (e.g., quantized or small-context model), the decision attaches an explainable reason and score. The runtime will annotate responses with route metadata for downstream billing and SLO traceability.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end latency improvement for p95 requests during network incidents compared to baseline region-only routing (target: reduce p95 by 15% during incidents).
- No more than 2x increase in fallback events compared to existing routing over a 7-day rolling window (safety limit while we iterate).
- Full decision trace emitted for 100% of routed requests (for sampling we will store details at 1% but expose real-time trace aggregation in Console).

Implementation plan (milestones):
- Spike: implement normalization & composite scoring in the telemetry pipeline, expose score stream (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/5982) — DONE 2025-11-24.
- Runtime hook: add GeoRouter decision step to serving runtime with hysteresis + decay controls (branch open: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/9147) — IN PROGRESS.
- Console: dashboard prototype for per-region weight and decision traces (Confluence doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENG/pages/308121/geo-router-design) — REVIEW.
- Canary: enable for internal traffic only, observe over 72h with automatic rollback on threshold breaches.

Tradeoffs & open questions:
- Coefficient tuning: initial alpha/beta/gamma are heuristic; we should run an offline sweep (historical incident replay) to find knee points.
- Storage vs. compute: per-region baselines require maintaining histograms; implement approximate TDigest to limit memory.
- Customer transparency vs. privacy: storing per-customer baselines helps personalization but increases storage and compliance complexity. For v1, keep baselines at region+tier level and revisit if per-customer analysis is required.

Testing strategy:
- Unit tests for normalization and composite formula.
- Synthetic chaos tests that inject packet-loss and RTO spikes into telemetry emulators.
- Replay tests against 30 days of historical telemetry to simulate incidents and validate hysteresis prevents flapping.

Observability & dashboarding:
- New Console tile: "Region Health Composite" with sparkline of composite weight, contributing signal breakdown, and "decision trace" links.
- Alerting rules: composite_weight > 0.8 for > 2m in >1 POP => Alert SRE (pager).

Progress updates / comments:
- 2025-11-19 (Sana Patel): Spike telemetry ingestion implemented and merged to telemetry staging. TDigest probe shows quantiles stable under load.
- 2025-11-25 (Liam O'Connor): Runtime hook prototype added; need input from Runtime team about adding a lightweight scoring path to avoid extra RPC. @Marisol Ruiz please review the library API.
- 2025-11-27 (Marisol Ruiz): Reviewed scoring API, requested that composite scoring be deterministic and have a "seeded tie-breaker" for identical weights to ensure route pinning for sticky sessions.
- 2025-11-30 (SRE team): Ran chaos test with 5% packet loss in europe-west; composite approach failed over to secondary POP with 70/30 split during confirmation window. Need to reduce confirmation window from 30s to 15s for low-latency workloads — action item recorded.
- 2025-12-02 (Liam O'Connor): Adjusted confirmation window to 20s and added a per-customer sensitivity multiplier to reduce unnecessary fallbacks for high-throughput customers. Updated PR.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- Offline parameter sweep (owner: Research/Applied ML) to find robust alpha/beta/gamma values.
- Implement TDigest-based baselining in production telemetry pipeline.
- Console: finalize visuals and add per-route cost annotation for cross-tier fallbacks.
- Security review: confirm that stored per-region baselines and decision traces comply with PII rules (task filed: SEC-842).
